fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (70%): ~$10.40 NTM EPS at Sept 2027 (consensus-derived, 4% execution haircut) x 25x = $260, and FCF yield (30%): ~$10.70/share NTM FCF at a 4% yield = $267. Blended ~$262, about 7% above the $244.04 close.

inputs_detail.value: $9.16 (29 analysts, range $8.28-$10.94, up from $8.80 90 days ago)

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus FY27 revenue $18.2B implies ~30% growth after 2026's ~31% organic; I step down to ~25% EPS growth in 2028, in line with Dell'Oro's low-20s% DCPI market growth into 2027 plus modest margin gains, supported by a $15B backlog (+~109%) and orders +152% organic in Q2, Nvidia guiding ~70% FY28 revenue growth, and third-party hyperscaler capex forecasts of ~$1T in 2027.

The Q2 revenue miss came from supply-chain congestion and project execution. Modine had the same supply constraints in its data center business, with 450-550bp of margin drag, so conversion friction looks industry-wide and may persist into 2027.

VRT trades ~26.6x FY27 consensus ($244.04/$9.16). Eaton trades ~26.8x FY27 ($431.41/$16.12) with slower growth, and nVent ~32x its 2026 EPS guide midpoint ($160.5/$5.05). A year from now, growth will be decelerating from ~30% toward the mid-20s and competition in liquid cooling is intensifying (Schneider/Motivair, Eaton/Boyd, Delta), so I apply a small discount to Eaton's forward multiple: 25x.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: NTM FCF at Sept 2027 ~$4.2B / 392.7M diluted shares = ~$10.70/share; 4.0% FCF yield

inputs_detail.derivation: Assumes FCF tracks adjusted EPS at ~100% conversion (2026: $2.5B FCF vs ~$2.64B adj. net income = $6.73 x 392.7M). Scaled with the NTM EPS path in method 1 (~$10.7/share), before the execution haircut.
The reciprocal of the 25x P/E used in method 1, consistent with the electrical-equipment peer multiples (Eaton ~27x FY27) and with ~100% cash conversion.

bear.story: AI capex digestion: hyperscalers guide 2027/28 capex flat or lower after investor pushback (as in the July 2026 Alphabet sell-off), order growth turns negative against tough comps, and the supply-chain friction seen at Vertiv and Modine hurts margins. NTM EPS gets cut to ~$8.50 and the multiple compresses to ~16-17x, as in cyclical capital-goods de-ratings. In 2022 VRT fell ~65% peak to trough.

base.story: Backlog of ~$15B converts as new Malaysia and Americas capacity comes online, Q3 guidance of 34-36% organic growth is met, and FY27 EPS lands near the $9.16 consensus. The DCPI market keeps growing in the low 20s% (Dell'Oro), but the multiple drifts to ~25x NTM as growth decelerates and liquid-cooling competition grows (Schneider/Motivair, Eaton/Boyd, Delta, nVent).

bull.story: Rubin/Kyber ramps (Nvidia guiding ~70% FY28 growth, $279B in supply commitments) and 2027 hyperscaler capex near $1T push orders and pricing higher. Execution normalizes, UIG adds grid-to-chip content, EPS beats (FY28 ~$13), and the stock re-rates to ~30x, back toward its 52-week high of ~$380.

thesis_break_reason: At ~$150 VRT would trade at ~16x FY27 consensus, below 60% of Eaton's multiple and near the 52-week low of ~$134-138. Given backlog of ~$15B and peers still reporting record data center orders, that level would most likely mean the market sees a real break: hyperscaler/neocloud order cancellations or deferrals, a sharp 2027 capex cut, a lasting loss of thermal share to Schneider/Eaton/Taiwan CDU vendors, or a recurring margin problem from execution failures. Ordinary 66%-vol noise would not explain it.

key_uncertainties: Durability of hyperscaler and neocloud capex into 2028. Third-party forecasts are ~$1T for 2027, but management teams have not guided and investors pushed back on capex in July 2026.
Whether the Q2 supply-chain and project-execution slip is transient. Modine showed similar industry-wide constraints.
Share in liquid cooling as Schneider (Motivair), Eaton (Boyd Thermal), nVent, Delta and other Taiwan ODM suppliers scale CDU capacity and Nvidia standardizes specs.
Order comparisons: organic orders +152% in Q2 2026 make 2027 order growth optically negative even if demand stays healthy.
Integration and earnout economics of the UIG acquisition.
Multiple: VRT trades at parity with Eaton on FY27 despite faster growth. Sentiment on AI infrastructure names can swing the multiple ±30%.
reasoning: The company-reported base: 2026 guide of $14.0B sales (+31% organic), adj. EPS $6.70, FCF ~$2.5B, backlog ~$15B, Q2 organic orders +152%. The stock fell ~35% from its high after a Q2 revenue miss blamed on supply chain and project execution. My lane is the value chain, and it mostly confirms demand. Dell'Oro has the DCPI market +28% in 1Q26 with thermal ~+50%, and expects low-20s% growth into early 2027. Eaton's Electrical Global backlog is +103%. Schneider raised guidance on data center strength, with Motivair growing fast and pricing up ~4 points. nVent more than doubled data center sales to ~$2B and is adding liquid-cooling capacity. Modine's data center sales are +90%. Nvidia printed $89B in data center revenue (+117%) and guided to ~70% FY28 growth. The chain also flags risks. Modine had the same supply-chain constraints and 450-550bp of margin drag, so execution friction is industry-wide. Competition in liquid cooling is intensifying: Schneider/Motivair launched a new CDU on 2026-09-23, Eaton bought Boyd Thermal, and Delta and other Taiwan suppliers sit on Nvidia's reference lists. Capex skepticism is also rising. On valuation, VRT at $244 is ~26.6x FY27 consensus of $9.16, roughly level with Eaton (~26.8x). A 25x multiple on ~$10.40 NTM EPS at the horizon gives ~$260, and FCF yield gives ~$267, for a blended fair value of ~$262 (+7%). My scenarios (bear $140 at 22%, base $265 at 50%, bull $380 at 28%) give a mean of ~$268 and a median near $250-255. For the ladder I used a lognormal centered at ~$255 with ~50% forward volatility, below the 66% realized figure, which was inflated by the drawdown after the Q2 miss. I then fattened the left tail slightly for an AI-capex digestion scenario, since VRT fell ~65% peak to trough in 2022. P(>=244) is ~0.535: a modest positive drift from strong value-chain demand, offset by decelerating growth, competition and multiple risk. No option data was used. The Manifold market on 2027 hyperscaler capex was checked but resolved N/A, so it adds no probability information. CNBC and the Eaton IR page blocked fetching, so I relied on search snippets and secondary coverage for those.
